ety.text: From Middle English sworen, isworen, from Old English sworen, ġesworen, from Proto-West Germanic *swaran, *giswaran, from Proto-Germanic *swaranaz, past participle of Proto-Germanic *swarjaną (“to swear”), equivalent to swear + -en.

ex: His sworn statement convinced the judge.

senses.d: Bound as though by an oath.
ex: Swum ashore, man, like a duck. I can swim like a duck, I'll be sworn.

chain.g: to confirm formally, to pronounce enforceably, to swear, to vow, to take an oath

ety.text: Inherited from West Midland Middle English sword (swerd in most dialects), from Old English sweord (“sword”), from Proto-West Germanic *swerd (“sword”), from Proto-Germanic *swerdą (“sword”), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *seh₂w- (“sharp”).

senses.d: A long bladed weapon with a grip and typically a pommel and crossguard (together forming a hilt), which is designed to cut, stab, slash and/or hack.
ex: He took out his sword and stabbed the man in the stomach.
